chunks: 3092 - And Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who forgot to slaughter in Minā until he visited the House, then he bought in Makkah and then slaughtered it. He said: “There is no harm; it has sufficed for him.”

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ: it sufficed and fulfilled the obligation
key_terms.بِمِنًى: in Minā, the prescribed location for this hajj rite
key_terms.زَارَ ٱلْبَيْتَ: visited the House, meaning the Kaʿbah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or problem in this case
key_terms.نَسِيَ: forgot or failed to remember the required act

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets to slaughter in Minā during hajj and does it later in Makkah, is it still valid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the sacrificial slaughter during hajj. If a person forgot to slaughter in Minā and only did so after going to the House and purchasing the animal in Makkah, the act is still valid and sufficient.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3092 - Muawiyah ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Abdullah (as)

regarding a man who forgot to slaughter in Mina until he visited the Kaaba, then purchased an animal in Mecca and slaughtered it.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm; it suffices for him."
